name: Dandin
dates_notes: Daṇḍin is commonly placed in the late seventh or early eighth century. The chronology and regional setting remain matters of scholarly reconstruction.
core_thesis: Daṇḍin's *Kāvyādarśa* is a formative account of poetic composition in which figures of speech are integrated with a broader analysis of stylistic qualities, defects, and regional modes of expression. His contribution is not a single exclusive essence of poetry, but a capacious practical theory of how verbal and semantic resources produce literary distinction. Later theorists of *rīti*, *dhvani*, and *rasa* inherit its classifications while arguing that style, suggestion, or aesthetic relish should receive greater theoretical priority.

engaged_works.title: Kavyadarsa
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: Conventionally placed in Daṇḍin's late-seventh- or early-eighth-century milieu.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Daṇḍin's principal treatise on poetics.

ascription_evidence.description: The Sanskrit poetics tradition and modern scholarship consistently attribute the Kāvyādarśa to Daṇḍin.

engaged_works.summary: A major early treatise on Sanskrit poetics in three chapters. It discusses the purposes and varieties of poetry, stylistic qualities and defects, regional literary modes, and a large taxonomy of figures. Its broad curricular influence made it a durable point of reference across South and Southeast Asia.
